title: Cultivated meat cost parity
bottleneck: Cultivated meat costs 5–10x conventional beef per kilogram by 2024 estimates, and the gap is structural: sterile bioreactors, pharmaceutical-grade growth media, and low cell densities make it an expensive way to grow protein. There is no existing manufacturing infrastructure to borrow — unlike plant-based, which uses food factories — so the industry must invent both the product and the factory simultaneously.
why_it_blocks: Without price parity, cultivated meat stays a luxury demo. Its climate and land-use benefits require mass adoption that cost prohibits. Without price parity, cultivated meat stays a luxury demo; its climate benefits require mass adoption cost prohibits.
current_state: A few products sell in Singapore and the US at premium prices; large-scale commercialization remains squarely in the future.
